name: American States Water
headline: A California water utility earning steady, regulator-approved returns, above those of its water-utility peers.
what_short: California water utility, plus electric and military water
what_it_does: American States Water supplies water to customers in southern California through its regulated Golden State Water subsidiary, which produces about 78% of sales. It also runs a small regulated electric utility in a wildfire-prone area and operates water systems on military bases under 50-year contracts.
why_it_passed: Customers have no other supplier, so the business is a regulated local monopoly with foreseeable earnings.
Its return on shareholders' equity averaged about 13.5% over ten years, above all three comparable water companies (about 7.6% to 9.5%) and above its own allowed 10.06%.
The state regulator authorized $573.1M of capital spending for 2025 to 2027, so the capital base on which it earns keeps growing.
Its allowed return (7.93% on the capital base) is set in public proceedings, which makes the next ten years easy to follow.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what this utility may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. The analysis values the shares at $49.86 to $54.71 against a price of $85.48. At that price the cash the business can pay out is only about 3.09% of the price, below the 5.30% a 30-year US Treasury bond pays.
watch: Water utilities in California can be held liable for fire damage even when they are not at fault, and its electric business serves a high wildfire-risk area.
All regulated operations are in southern California, so one event such as an earthquake could affect the whole business.
About $106M is owed by the US government to its military-contract business.
